rationale: The observed continuation is a plausible noun-object after “took the,” but pears receives little probability despite the existing preceding_verb_surface feature. Batch documents also include pears as an object after different verbs and in other contexts, so this is not evidence for a general rule that every “took the” must be followed by pears. Add modest, narrowly matched evidence for pears when the visible prefix records a preceding verb of “took.” No new head is needed because the current head already exposes that feature. This may disadvantage other valid objects after “took,” including scissors; the small added weight preserves that uncertainty. The unprompted sample is diagnostic rather than a training target, and this provisional patch has not passed replay gating.
